characters.name: Clerk Sena
characters.role: Keeper of the council’s working record

dialogue.speaker: water-keeper
dialogue.text: The drought turn starts here. Our gate model takes twelve buckets. Two drain away before the split. See where the water goes with two different settings. The farm and lower crews have left notes about the work they need done.

dialogue.speaker: water-keeper
dialogue.text: Sena pinned the first turn in the council room. The repair crew has left its report there. Bring its note back before we fit the gate for a fresh trial.

dialogue.speaker: water-keeper
dialogue.text: The crew closed the leak. We can run twelve incoming buckets again. Keep a gate setting from the drought run and use it first. Then try another setting with the seal fitted.

options.text: Fit the repaired gate and keep the same incoming count.
Leave the repair board here a moment.
I followed the water’s route at the Emberford washhouse.

dialogue.speaker: water-keeper
dialogue.text: The model now keeps the two buckets that leaked before. Reopen the gate board with the setting from the first order. Write that count beside the drought count and try a second position.

dialogue.speaker: water-keeper
dialogue.text: Twelve come in on both boards. Use the old setting on the repaired gate once, then try a different position. The old readings stay at the gate for checking.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: Six buckets cover the named rows at the morning bell. The lower workshop’s five cover the first fetching round. Read both slips where the crews work. Bring the two gate runs so we can see which jobs the measured supply can cover.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: Six for the rows and five for the lower work would take eleven. With twelve in and two lost, our drought trial lets ten reach the crews. Pick an order for this intake and these work cards. Sena leaves space for another count if the intake slips or a crew adds a round.

options.text: Send seven to the rows and three to the lower channel.
Split it five and five. Delay a bucket of the field work.
Give the lower channel seven so it can hold two in reserve.
Leave the first order open.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The first order is on the wall. The report from the repair crew is on a separate sheet here. Read it, then meet Omi at the gate.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The repair gives us a fresh reading. A new heading by the old order says we agreed on both daily marks. Look at the heading and the numbers underneath it. Bring the old setting repeated under repair and one other repaired run. The market kept two figures side by side for different questions. Here a request and a delivery need separate lines, too.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The same setting now sends two more buckets past the sealed leak. Other settings can send still more to the lower channel while the rows wait. Pick a tested repaired order. The old result will stay below its own date.

options.text: Run the repaired gate for the rows and the usual lower rounds.
Keep two more in the lower channel. Leave one bucket of row work for later.
Send the repaired flow first to the lower channel and record the paused rows.
Leave both readings ready.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: Both turns have their own dates. The old requests were goals for those crews on that day. We can give the old and new orders more room so a reader sees each beside its work card.

options.text: Leave a wider register copy beside the council seats.
Keep the records open.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The new copy gives the drought result, repair result and requests their own rows. Someone at the seats can follow the order without putting a finger over the earlier numbers.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: A field worker copied the paused rows. A lower worker checked the reserve. The dates on their two slips will tell us which gate each used.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The field crew can start its marked rows. The lower crew has three buckets. Work that needs its last two buckets has to wait. Sena keeps the lower request beside the order. She files it under twelve incoming and two lost.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The drought line says seven to the rows and three to the channel. Six and five were the two requests. We recorded a setting that put the rows first while the gate leaked. Keep the request and the result on different lines.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: Seven buckets reach the rows and five reach the lower channel. Both groups can do the work on their notes. Sena leaves the earlier shortage visible. A lower crew that wants extra in reserve will need another agreement.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The lower crew can do the work on its fetching list. The field crew marks the row that has to wait for its sixth bucket. Sena puts the two stops beside the split. She files it under twelve incoming and two lost.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The drought line reads five to the rows and five to the channel. Equal shares left one bucket of row work waiting. The later writer read equal shares as both jobs finished. The work cards have their own counts.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The row work still has five buckets. The lower crew now gets seven. It can hold two above the usual five. Sena adds the postponed work beside the new reserve in the register.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The lower crew can hold two beyond its usual five. The field crew gets three of its six and changes which rows it prepares. Sena leaves that cost next to the order. She files it under twelve incoming and two lost.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The drought line gives three to the rows and seven to the lower channel. We chose a reserve for that crew and left field rows waiting. The phrase “both daily marks” belongs to the requests beside it.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: The lower crew gets nine, four above its usual five. Three buckets reach the rows and three of their work-card buckets still wait. The new order shows both the reserve and the work that moves to a later turn.

dialogue.speaker: water-keeper
dialogue.text: At the washhouse you kept the head peg in view and checked where the water went again. Here our head count is twelve on both pages. Repeat your chosen setting under repair and see which outlet gets the two buckets we kept.

options.text: Fit the repaired gate and keep the same incoming count.
Leave the repair board here a moment.

dialogue.speaker: water-keeper
dialogue.text: Good. Bring the notebook to the clear patch above this peg. The water makes plenty of noise at the lower bank. Find the place that lets a person see the mark, or keep the time and name on whatever reading the keeper left.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The notebook brings the peg’s little foot line into view. At the noon bell Omi sees three intervals from that line. Clip the standing place to the new space on the page.

options.text: Clip the upper peg’s noon reading with Omi’s name.
Leave the sheet by the upper peg.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The upper note now holds the peg, its foot line and the noon bell. The lower bank has its own sightline.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You can hear the channel here. A thick patch of reeds covers the lower peg. The notebook leaves room for a different standing place or a dated handover.

options.text: Mark the covered noon view and look for another way to check.
Leave the reed-side box open.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The high step east of the reeds gives you a clear line. The lower crew’s handover on the west terrace holds an earlier reading. Choose what you can keep with its date.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: From the high step the reeds fall below the sightline. You can see two notch intervals above the foot of the lower peg during the noon bell. The foot belongs to this peg.

options.text: Clip the noon reading to the high-step drawing.
Leave room for the crew’s earlier handover.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The two noon views can sit side by side with their separate foot lines. The blank from behind the reeds stays in the notes.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The lower keeper has signed a reading of two intervals from the lower peg’s foot at the previous bell. Slide the signed time under the clip and leave the place for noon open.

options.text: Clip the handover with its keeper and earlier bell.
Leave room for the view from the high step.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The handover gives a reading for the earlier bell. Leave the noon square for another keeper. Both local times stay on the page.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: Bring the upper reading and the lower note. Each has its own foot line. A single copy lets a reader hold the two lines together. Local copies let each crew check beside its peg. Leave a mark on the short crew track so the next reader can carry either copy between them.

options.text: Mount both dated records at the council.
Leave each reader’s note beside its own peg.
Leave the clips by the board.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: I’ll leave the two foot lines and both times on one board. Anyone who needs the lower bank can follow the short observer track with the notebook open.

dialogue.speaker: water-scribe
dialogue.text: I’ll leave a copy at each peg so the crews can match a line to the place. The short observer track gives a reader a way to carry the two dates between them.

missions.title: The Agreement at the Weir
missions.knowledgeQuestion: How can a shared rule stay fair when a measurement and the conditions change?
missions.stake: If the drought plan hides who loses, one crew's fields fail and nobody owns the choice.

objectives.title: Cross to the Water Commons and find the gate.
Try two gate settings in the drought model.

kq.action: compare routes with the same incoming count

objectives.title: Read the work-card needs for the marked rows and lower channel.

kq.action: check why each crew uses its mark

objectives.title: Give Sena the first gate order and record the work that will wait.

kq.action: make a water order with two work cards

objectives.title: Read the repair report and help Omi fit the repaired gate.
Repeat the first setting under repair and try one other repaired run.

kq.action: repeat one setting before and after a repair

objectives.title: Read the new heading above the original drought order.

kq.action: compare an old agreement with its new heading

objectives.title: With Sena, keep the original order and add a supported repair order.

kq.action: correct a public account while keeping the earlier result

missions.title: Two Rows in the Register
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What makes a record usable to people whose work depends on it?

objectives.title: Give both orders more room on Sena’s register copy.

missions.title: Room in the Relief Basin
missions.knowledgeQuestion: What can a route model tell us about a spare bucket, and who should get it?
missions.stake: The crew has one wide tile before the heavier practice pulse. The new seed beds and the lower troughs both need room.

objectives.title: Bring the seed terrace’s and lower crew’s relief slips to Omi’s bench.
Release the heavier pulse with the wide tile in each socket.
Fit a tested relief layout and check the outlet on the lower path.

missions.title: The Bell Behind the Reeds
missions.knowledgeQuestion: When can different readings sit together, and which conditions have to stay with them?
missions.stake: Omi wants a reader on the lower bank to know whose mark they can use and when it was checked.

objectives.title: With the notebook open, check the upper peg and find a usable lower record.
Put the dated peg readings beside each other or beside their own banks.
Use the notebook’s marked observer track between the lower bank and Council Yard.

missions.title: Three Messengers
missions.knowledgeQuestion: When do two reports supply two independent checks?
missions.stake: The lower crew needs a fresh spill-line check after the bell. A repeated message can make the earlier check sound new.

objectives.title: Find Omi’s original and copy, then the lower crew’s own check.
Fit the source clip and replay both runner orders at the council counter.
Post a check request or leave the docket, then visit the chosen display.

missions.title: Before the Next Count
missions.stake: A runner needs to know when the council order can go out as written.
missions.knowledgeQuestion: When does an old count still support the next order?

objectives.title: Check where Sena has left the intake slip.

hints.text: A gate and council passage has opened in the Nexus.
Look for the Water Commons sign beside the other crossings.
Go through and follow the path to the central gate board.
Omi stands by the board in the Gatehouse. You can try it before the council meets.
Two of the incoming buckets drain away before either crew can use them.
Find the gate board by Omi in the Gatehouse.
Choose two different settings and watch what reaches each side.
Use the fields, split or channel controls. Take two distinct readings to Sena.
Each crew left a count that belongs to its work today.
Go to the farm and lower channel district.
Read the farm’s work card by the rows and the lower crew’s marker farther along the channel.
Keep six buckets for the marked rows and five for the lower work in view as you take both notes to the council.
The two work cards ask for eleven with only ten reaching the outlets.
Speak with Sena after reading both cards and trying two drought settings.
Choose a tested setting and keep the shortfall or reserve on its line.
Set the first order at the council. The report for the repaired gate then appears nearby.
The crew has left a report about the part that drained away.
Look for the repair report in the council room after the first order.
Read it before talking to Omi again at the Gatehouse.
Tell Omi to fit the repaired gate. The board can now make another twelve-bucket run.
Repeat your first setting before comparing with another.
Use the repaired gate board. The drought readings stay beside it.
Select whichever setting you published for the drought first.
Run the published setting and one other under repair. Compare the same setting across the two conditions.
A new heading claims the old order met both work cards.
Look by the original order in the council room after fitting the repair.
Read the new heading and check the older figures on its page.
Take the disputed slip to Sena with the repeated gate readings.
Keep the two orders on their own dates.
After comparing the repaired readings, talk to Sena about the draft heading.
Check what the old setting did in each condition, then choose a setting you actually tried under repair.
Give Sena a supported repair order. Its work-card consequence appears beside the preserved drought line.
A reader wants to follow the old order and the repair without swapping them.
Speak with Sena after the repaired order appears.
Ask her to give the two dates and the work cards more room.
Choose the wider register copy, then look for it beside the council seats.
Omi’s relief bench needs the two local requests.
Both slips are on the lower path. One is by the seed beds and one is across the boards on the lower bank.
Read the relief slip at each outlet. Each has a request for this smaller trial.
From the Old Weir use the lower path. Read the seed terrace’s relief slip and the lower crew’s relief slip. Return to Omi’s bench.
The bench has one wide tile and two sockets.
A plain layout can show why the basin matters. Try the same eight buckets with the wide piece at each outlet.
Place the piece at the seed rows and release eight. Move the same piece to the lower channel and release eight.
Read rows, lower channel, basin, and spill after both eight-bucket trials. The two arrangements leave different requests waiting.
Choose a layout for Omi to fit. Keep the other report open.
Your trial tested the same pulse for both placements. Each widened one branch.
Place the wide tile at the chosen outlet then use Fit this relief layout.
Fit the layout and visit its new wide relief mouth on the lower path. The seed outlet is west of the boards. The lower outlet is east.
Open Elian’s notebook in your Bag at the Old Weir.
The upper peg is by the clear path at the gate. Follow the lower path to the reeds at the second peg.
Clip Omi’s noon reading and mark the blocked view at the reeds. Check the high step or the earlier crew handover.
Use upper peg, reeds, and one of high step east or crew log west. Keep the time attached to whichever lower record you choose.
Sena has a board for both peg notes at the Council Yard.
Bring the two dated records to Sena’s copy board beside the register.
You can put both records together or place a copy near each peg.
Use Sena’s copy board and pick a place for the records. The chosen copies keep the standing place, foot line and bell.
Use the marked observer track with the notebook open.
Look for the new trail sign west in the Council Yard or south on the lower bank.
The new track links both ways. The usual paths still carry you when you close the notebook.
Use the marked track from the Council Yard or from the lower-bank bend. Then view the copy wherever you placed it.
The old Forest counter method can travel with the rehearsal slips.
Omi’s slip and its council copy sit near the upper rail. The lower crew has its own slip across the boards.
Read who checked each view, then see who carried it. Add the lower crew’s separate observation.
Near Omi read the rehearsal slip and council copy. At the lower bank read the lower crew’s independently written check.
The council counter keeps runners and observers in different places.
Fit the source clip. Try the first bundle where Omi’s slip comes first, then the return bundle where his copy arrives first.
Run all three packets in each bundle. Each of the two independent checks records zero.
Check why the origin count stays at two even when three people deliver a packet. Keep the after-bell slot open.
Choose where the next watcher can see the open check.
A bank marker is close to the channel. A docket carries both observer names in the Council Yard.
Use the selected display on the lower path or by the council bench.
Read the bank marker if you put up the request, or read the docket in the council if you kept the handover there. The board can move the display again.
The next runner needs to know which count goes with this order.
Look in the Council Yard after posting the drought order.
Check either the intake mark by the runner or the blank tally at the steps. It follows the notice you left at the Market.
Read the intake mark near the centre path or the blank tally at the east steps. Each shows what the runner should do if the intake changes.

journal.text: The same setting gives a different lower count after the leak is closed. We kept the drought order and the new order beside their own readings and work cards.
We sent the same pulse through two layouts. The basin showed what neither route took. Omi left the unmet request with the chosen piece so the next crew could see what still needed room.
We kept a gap for the lower peg’s covered view. The follow-up kept the reading beside the time and standing place that made it possible. The path lets the crews carry those conditions with the copy.

Sena’s packet came from Omi’s own rehearsal slip. The lower crew’s zero came from a different check. Both reading places stay beside the two source names, and the after-bell slot is ready for a fresh check.

moments.did: You kept both crews’ work in view when there was too little water for both requests.
moments.prompt: Where did you leave the work that had to wait?

moments.did: You repeated a gate setting after the repair so you could compare the two conditions.
moments.prompt: What made the earlier run a useful comparison?

moments.did: You corrected the heading while keeping the original decision in the record.
moments.prompt: What would a later reader learn from keeping both dates?

chronicle.title: The first gate order
chronicle.text: Two work cards went into the decision. The chosen drought order kept its delayed work in view.

chronicle.title: Twelve buckets again
chronicle.text: The repair changed what reached the lower channel. The council kept both orders and corrected the later heading.

keepsakeTalks.text: Show Elian’s notebook and ask where this peg can be read.
